A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same FideDiff study, and all 13 pages support reliable text and visual comparison. Neither includes appendices or embedded supplements; supplementary material referenced in the text is outside the supplied evidence.

before.justification: v2 reports original FideDiff benchmark results, inference timings, and ablations in Section 5 and Tables 2–7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, inference timings, and ablations in Section 5 and Tables 2–7.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the identical consistency-training procedure, diffusion foundation model, Kernel ControlNet, timestep prediction, losses, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same original and enlarged GoPro training data and evaluate motion deblurring on GoPro, HIDE, RealBlur-J, and RealBlur-R.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout. Table 2 retains Restormer, HI-Diff, UFPNet, AdaRevD, DiffBIR, OSEDiff, Diff-Plugin, and UID-Diff; the timing and ablation comparisons also match.

E3.justification: Dataset counts, evaluation metrics, model configurations, training stages, input resizing, and inference timestep settings are identical, including the protocols for the ablations and fair comparison.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 retains the same foundation-model, Kernel ControlNet, consistency-training, timestep-prediction, and training-data analyses. The timestep sensitivity plots and visual examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported experiments.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 2 reports FideDiff GoPro PSNR of 28.79 and LPIPS of 0.0831 in both versions; Table 3 retains its 1.52-second GoPro inference time.

T1.justification: The diffusion preliminaries, blur-process formulation, consistency objective, kernel-conditioning equations, and loss definitions are identical, including Equations 1–13.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about single-step high-fidelity deblurring, consistency training, Kernel ControlNet, adaptive timestep prediction, and comparative performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of fidelity, generalization, and timestep robustness are unchanged. Both retain the same discussion of VAE detail loss, the speed-quality tradeoff, and GPU memory constraints.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same Stable Diffusion 2.1 backbone, LoRA training, resizing procedure, and four A800-80GB GPUs. The code/data release statement and references to supplementary implementation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior diffusion and deblurring methods are identical.

P1.justification: On page 1, Jiezhang Cao’s affiliation marker changes from 2 to 1,2, adding Shanghai Jiao Tong University alongside Harvard University. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–7, their captions, and document layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–13 are pixel-identical; page 1 differences are confined to the affiliation text and version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 updates an author affiliation and the version/date stamp while preserving the scientific content, evidence, explanations, and visual presentation. These administrative edits do not meaningfully change the paper’s overall quality.
